newsitem.title: USA: Oregon independents push to trim large retailers.
newsitem.headline: Oregon independents push to trim large retailers.

text.p: Oregon's independent gasoline dealers will ask lawmakers Thursday to support a bill scaling back the number of stations operated by big oil companies statewide, said a representative for the dealers.

Members of the Oregon Gasoline Dealers Association are pushing for passage of the Oregon Equity and Competition Act because they fear the ongoing consolidation of West Coast refining and marketing will squeeze them out of business.
"Independents" act as franchisers, leasing stations from major oil companies but choosing the gasoline suppliers they want.
"(Majors) decided they want control at every level...and the independents get in the way of that," said Len Bergstein, a lobbyist and spokesman for the association.
A lobbyist for oil companies was not immediately available for comment.
Representatives of independent dealers and oil companies will give an hour's testimony before the state's Senate Civil Law, Business, Labor and Government Operations Committee late Thursday.
Bergstein said hundreds of supporters would watch the proceedings and present lawmakers with a 20,000-signature petition supporting the bill, also known as SB 400.
Four other states, including Maryland and Nevada, have passed laws similar to SB 400, and Hawaii lawmakers are in the midst of such approving such legislature.
Atlantic Richfield Co. (ARCO), Tosco Corp, Shell Oil Co. and Chevron Corp are major players in the Oregon retail gasoline market.
